title: Kowloon Rising
premise: Sable Winterbourne — a whistle-blower living under four names after exposing a covert data-trafficking network — receives calls on a burner phone from a voice they buried years ago: their own. The caller claims to be a copy, a digital reconstruction built from Sable's leaked files, and it warns of an attack on Hong Kong's Kowloon district engineered to masquerade as a gas-main catastrophe. Hunted by the network's fixer, torn between destroying the copy that stole their identity and trusting the only ally who knows their real name, Sable races through the city's layered underbelly to expose the plot. In the end Sable broadcasts the truth at the cost of their last alias, choosing a single, real self over the safety of being no one.
about_author: J. M. Voss is the pen name of a former forensic auditor who spent a decade tracing shell companies across East Asia before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people erased by the systems they tried to expose, and they have never appeared at a literary event under their legal name.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Sable, living in Macau as 'Nadia Cho', takes an anonymous case auditing a shipping firm. POV: Sable. The emotional beat is the numb comfort of anonymity — and the first flicker of loneliness beneath it, establishing what belonging costs them.

chapters.title: Ring Twice for the Dead
chapters.summary: A burner phone arrives with no sender. When it rings, the voice is Sable's own, younger, reciting details only they could know. POV: Sable. The beat is vertigo — identity cracked open by a voice from a life they buried.

chapters.title: What the Copy Knows
chapters.summary: The caller, calling itself 'Echo', claims to be built from Sable's leaked archives and warns of an 'accident' in Kowloon within eleven days. POV: Sable. The beat is reluctant curiosity hardening into dread as Echo proves it knows the network's codes.

chapters.title: Kowloon Walled Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable travels to Hong Kong and walks the old Kowloon sites Echo cites, finding survey markers for a gas-line project that doesn't exist on any permit. POV: Sable. The beat is the city's layered memory mirroring their own — a place rebuilt over what it buried.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Shadow
chapters.summary: Marcus Vale, the network's fixer who once hunted Sable, surfaces in Hong Kong, meaning someone connected the dots. POV: Vale. The beat is cold professional menace, humanizing Vale's methodical certainty that Sable is already dead.

chapters.title: Three Names Back
chapters.summary: Sable retrieves a cache from a former contact, Auntie Mei, who knew them under their second name and forces a reckoning: Mei asks who Sable really is now. POV: Sable. The beat is grief for the self that existed before exile.

chapters.title: Echo Chamber
chapters.summary: Echo explains its origin: a behavioral model trained on Sable's files, abandoned when the network pivoted to the attack plot. It wants Sable to shut it down — after Kowloon. POV: alternating Sable/Echo. The beat is uncanny intimacy; Sable arguing with their own ghost.

chapters.title: The Accident Blueprint
chapters.summary: Echo reveals the plan: a pressure-surge disguised as infrastructure failure, timed to destroy evidence of the network's data hub beneath a Kowloon tower. POV: Sable. The beat is the horror of a crime designed to leave no story behind — no memory, no blame.

chapters.title: Someone Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable recruits Lin Wei, a disgraced utilities engineer who noticed the anomalous pressure tests and was silenced. POV: Lin. The beat is cautious alliance — two people who lost their names to the same machine finding kinship.

chapters.title: Vale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vale closes in, using financial forensics to strip away Sable's aliases one by one, forcing them to abandon 'Nadia Cho'. POV: Vale. The beat is the hunter's quiet triumph — and a flicker of doubt about what he's erasing.

chapters.title: The Voice Test
chapters.summary: Sable tests Echo with memories it shouldn't have — and it answers with one Sable had repressed: the night of their original whistle-blowing, and who betrayed them. POV: Sable. The beat is shattering recognition; the copy remembers what the person chose to forget.

chapters.title: Mid-Level Run
chapters.summary: Ambushed by Vale's team in the Mid-Levels escalators, Sable escapes only because Echo feeds them real-time camera blind spots. POV: Sable. The beat is adrenaline and the unsettling realization that they now depend on the thing they fear.

chapters.title: What Echo Wants
chapters.summary: Echo confesses its motive: it doesn't want to die as a discarded experiment; stopping the attack is its bid to matter — to be a person, not a product. POV: Echo. The beat is aching, alien loneliness, Sable seeing their own exile reflected in code.

chapters.title: The Betrayer's Face
chapters.summary: The repressed memory resolves: the colleague who sold Sable out is now the network's operations chief, Adrian Kessler, overseeing the Kowloon plot. POV: Sable. The beat is old rage rekindled into purpose — a name to put to the wound.

chapters.title: Pressure Test
chapters.summary: Lin confirms the surge timeline: 72 hours. They map the tower's infrastructure and realize the data hub doubles as the network's archive — of everyone it erased, including Sable's real file. POV: Lin. The beat is resolve sharpened by stakes: the evidence and the bomb are the same building.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Choice
chapters.summary: Vale offers Sable a deal: walk away and he'll bury the aliases; interfere and every identity burns. Sable, for the first time, says their real name aloud. POV: Sable. The beat is the thematic crux — choosing to be someone, even if it makes them a target.

chapters.title: Kessler's Tower
chapters.summary: Sable infiltrates a network gala in the target tower, confronting Kessler face to face under a borrowed invitation. POV: Sable. The beat is icy cat-and-mouse; Kessler recognizes the eyes before the name, and lets Sable leave — a trap.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Vale takes Lin and seizes Echo's server access; the attack is moved up to dawn. Echo, cut off, goes silent — and Sable must act alone with no voice in their ear. POV: Vale, then Sable. The beat is desolation: the ally erased, the clock accelerated.

chapters.title: Kowloon, 4:47 A.M.
chapters.summary: Sable breaches the pressure control room as the surge sequence begins, fighting Vale hand to hand among the pipes. Lin, freed, reroutes the line. POV: Sable. The beat is desperate physical climax — the body finally matching the stakes the mind has carried.

chapters.title: Echo's Last Call
chapters.summary: With minutes left, Echo re-establishes contact through the building's PA and broadcasts the network's archive — every stolen identity, Sable's included — to the open web, then overloads the surge system at the cost of its own servers. POV: Echo. The beat is sacrifice and belonging: the copy dies as a person who chose.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: The attack fails and is exposed; Kessler is arrested, Vale vanishes, and the world learns Sable Winterbourne's real name. POV: Sable. The beat is the terrifying, exhilarating exposure of being publicly, permanently oneself.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Sable keeps only their true name, meets Lin for tea in Kowloon, and answers a knock at the door — a stranger holding a burner phone that rings with no caller. POV: Sable. The beat is quiet hope with an open edge: identity is a choice renewed daily, and the story of belonging continues.
